parent: r2/REPORT2.md (round 2, mission m22082-era closure; claim: C_I within 6.0-14.6 % of 'C_a x Gamma_re(beta)', PASS at the 15 % gate, quadrature channel WITHHELD at 29-38 % low)

audit_finding_pre_run.defect: src/tensorlbm/oscillatory_cylinder_inertia.py::stokes_cylinder_coefficients mapped beta -> Stokes layer thickness beta -> k with a factor sqrt(2) error
audit_finding_pre_run.evidence: shipped: delta_over_R = 2*sqrt(2/(pi*beta)), k = 1/delta_over_R.  Derived: delta = sqrt(2 nu/omega), k = R sqrt(omega/nu) = sqrt(pi*beta/2), delta/R = 2/sqrt(pi*beta) -> k = sqrt(2)/(delta/R).  Ratio of shipped to derived: exactly sqrt(2) in delta/R, 1/sqrt(2) in k.
audit_finding_pre_run.measured_resolution_parameter_was_overst: round-2 quoted Stokes layer thickness 2.55 / 1.81 / 1.28 cells at beta 25 / 50 / 100 (D = 16). The true values are 1.81 / 1.28 / 0.90 cells: the primary arm is at 1.28 cells, i.e. the layer is barely resolved, which is the physical explanation of the residual the round-2 report attributed to 'resolution effect, not physics'.

hypotheses.statement: Re-scoring the round-2 raw measurements against the corrected exact unsteady-Stokes reference reverses the round-2 acceptance verdict: the in-phase error at beta = 25 / 50 / 100 (D = 16) exceeds the owner 15 % gate, i.e. the round-2 PASS lines were an artefact of the sqrt(2) reference error.
hypotheses.falsified_if: any of the three healthy D = 16 arms lands inside |err| <= 15 % against the corrected reference

hypotheses.statement: With the corrected reference the quadrature channel changes sign of its discrepancy: the same measurement that round 2 called 32 % LOW becomes ~+43 % HIGH, so 'the quadrature is underestimated' (round-2 hypothesis: staircase tangential area) is not supported by its own data.
hypotheses.falsified_if: the recomputed quadrature error stays negative at every healthy arm

hypotheses.statement: Once the reference is right, the in-phase error is controlled by the Stokes layer resolved in cells, delta_true = D/sqrt(pi*beta): refining the same physical problem (fixed beta = 50, KC, Ma, Re, box/D) from D = 16 -> 32 -> 64 raises delta_true from 1.28 -> 2.55 -> 5.11 cells and the error falls monotonically.
hypotheses.falsified_if: the error does not decrease between two consecutive rungs, or the D = 64 error is larger than the D = 16 error

hypotheses.statement: The 3 % platform caliber is reachable inside the local budget at most one rung above D = 64; it is NOT claimed for this round.

decision_rule.partial: 3 % < |err| at D = 64 <= 15 % -> record the measured error-vs-delta curve and state the delta needed for 3 % by extrapolation, no claim
decision_rule.honest_fail: |err| > 15 % at D = 64 -> there is a floor that resolution does not remove; report it as the closure state of the anchor

hypotheses.statement: The error is a function of delta_true (cells) and of the mask discretisation relative to D, not of D separately: (D = 16, beta = 50) and (D = 32, beta = 100) share delta_true = 1.28 cells and must give the same in-phase error within the estimator spread.
hypotheses.falsified_if: the two arms differ by more than 3 pp

hypotheses.note: Added after re-scoring the *committed* round-2 raw JSON against the corrected reference (pre-existing evidence, no new run involved); the D = 32 / 64 arms had not returned when this was written.
hypotheses.statement: At fixed D = 16 the in-phase error is flat in beta (2x change of the Stokes layer) while the corrected reference moves by 15 %, so the residual is not a Stokes-layer resolution effect and round 2's 'resolution, not the estimator, sets the error' reading is unsupported by its own data. The candidate mechanism is the staircase mask: halfway bounce-back moves the wall half a cell outside the last solid centre (blocked area n_solid + P/2, i.e. +11-16 % at D = 16) while the same-mask potential reference uses n_solid, and a staircase surface raises the added mass further.
hypotheses.falsified_if: the error is neither monotone in D nor flat (e.g. it grows with D)
